content:
lee: Heads up — small-batch decode p50/p99 and overall throughput regressed after yesterday's fused-flash patch. CI perf run attached, looks bad for batch sizes 1-4. Can someone sanity-check kernel selection fallback?
priya: Which model + seq lengths? CI run id?
lee: gpt-medium, max_seq 2048. Typical decode traffic is batch_size 1-3, avg prompt len ~600. CI run perf id perf-run/763. Summary from run: p50 +18%, p99 +32%, throughput -12% at low QPS.
sam: I grabbed perf samples from the canary. Flamegraph shows attention_unpack and memcpy dominating on decode. My quick hypothesis: paged->fused change introduced extra mem ops for small KV pages (unaligned copies).
lee: Interesting. I also see an increase in host-to-device memcpy time in the logs around the attention kernel call.
perf-bot: Attached artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/perf/763/flame.svg and https://artifacts.internal/perf/763/trace.json :eyes:
jon: Can we force the legacy paged-flash kernel in staging to verify? If latency returns to baseline we can blame selector heuristics.
lee: Yes — you can force via env toggle on the runtime: 
```
REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=legacy_paged
./deploy-canary --service=runtime --canary=small-decode
```
priya: Pushed the toggle to staging. Running the same microbench harness now.
priya: Quick results: after forcing legacy_paged, p50/p99 are back within 3% of baseline. Throughput recovered. So selector picked fused variant for small decode and that path regressed.
sam: That matches my perf samples. Fused path has extra path that does a page-aligning memcpy for KV pages < 512 bytes. For small-batch decode we hit that often.
jon: Two actionable items: 1) change default selector to prefer paged for batch_size <=4 and avg_seq >=512; 2) add a microbenchmark that exercises small-batch decode with tiny KV pages to catch regression.
lee: Agreed. I'll open a PR for selector heuristic + unit perf test. Will also add a runtime flag to prefer fused only for large batches/long-context.
infra-bot: deploy-canary started: runtime/canary/764.
perf-bot: CI perf job queued: perf-run/764 (compare vs 763).
lee: Thanks. Also adding alert rule: if decode p99 regresses >20% vs baseline for 1h, notify #eng-runtime and create perf ticket automatically.
sam: FYI I'll prototype a cheaper path in fused implementation to avoid memcpy for small pages — might be another fix if selector change isn't ideal.
lee: Perfect. I'll post the PR link and attach perf diffs when ready. :thumbsup:
